description: This command is available for PFC only. It can be used to convert data files written in PFC 5.0 to be compatible with PFC 6.0 . If s is specified, it must correspond to an existing file name, and this file will be converted. The original file is not altered, and a converted file is created that retains the name of the original file and is placed in the folder './out/' by default. This default behavior may be changed with the following keywords.

keywords.name: directory
keywords.description: If specified, all the files located in the direcory s will be converted. This keyword cannot be used in conjonction with file and output-file .

keywords.name: file
keywords.description: If specified, the name of the file to be converted is set to s .

keywords.name: output-directory
keywords.description: If specified, the name of the output directory where the converted file(s) are created is set to s .

keywords.name: output-file
keywords.description: If specified, the name of the output file is set to s .

keywords.name: prefix
keywords.description: If specified, the name of the new, converted file is set to the name of the original file prefixed with the string s .

keywords.name: suffix
keywords.description: If specified, the name of the new, converted file is set to the name of the original file suffixed with the string s .

keywords.name: safe
keywords.description: Activate/Deactivate safe conversion of FISH variables. If set to true (default), then FISH variables are expected to start with the @ symbol.

examples.description: Convert one PFC 5.0 data file to 6.0 syntax

notes: PFC only: converts data files written for PFC 5.0 to PFC 6.0 syntax.
Removed after 6.0: convert is absent from the 7.00/9.8 program enumerations.
With no file or directory argument it converts every data file in the current directory - mind your working directory before running the bare form.
verification: Live-verified 2026-11-10 on the PFC2D/PFC3D 6.00 consoles (syntax grade): convert is in the 6.00 program enumeration and "program convert file '<missing>'" parses through to a file-open error; the convert token itself is rejected on 7.00/9.8. The bare (convert-everything) form was never run.
